title: `celery inspect`, `celery control` and `celery events` all traceback on cluster failures
title_original: Fix#9722 friendly status errors for CLI
text_original:
### Summary

Thanks @harshang03 for the awesome work on #10118! The UX improvement for CLI broker errors is fantastic and much needed.

I noticed that Codecov reported some missing coverage and @auvipy requested additional tests. Since the PR hasn't been updated in about a month, I went ahead and added the missing unit tests to cover the remaining `try...except` blocks to help get this over the finish line.

### What was added
Added unit tests to simulate `OperationalError` and unexpected exceptions for the following commands, ensuring the `handle_remote_command_error` is triggered correctly:
- [x] `celery inspect <command>` 
- [x] `celery control <command>` (broadcast)
- [x] `celery events` (covering the `_run_evcam` and `_run_evtop` paths)

---
issue https://github.com/celery/celery/issues/9722
text_rewritten: The remote-control commands share the rough edge `celery status` has: any failure while talking to the cluster escapes as a raw Python traceback. That covers both a broker that is unreachable and an unexpected error raised further down the call. Every command that talks to the cluster should turn the failure into a command-level error -- exit EX_UNAVAILABLE, print one line naming the command and the underlying reason, print no traceback. A cluster that is reachable but silent keeps its existing 'no nodes replied' outcome, and successful invocations keep printing their replies unchanged.

acceptance_hint: `celery inspect`, `celery control` and `celery events` exit EX_UNAVAILABLE with the underlying reason and no traceback for both transport failures and unexpected exceptions, while successful runs are unaffected.
